nodes.description: High-output cardiac failure driven by hepatic arteriovenous shunting. It was the commonest non-fatal comorbidity in a cohort of deceased HHT patients (69%) and the second commonest cause of death (26%). Symptomatic hepatic AVMs are managed medically, with liver transplantation reserved for refractory high-output failure. Because the hepatic lesion burden is greater in HHT2, this is not an HHT1-predominant manifestation, but it does occur in HHT1 and is the mechanism connecting the hepatic lesion to mortality.

evidence.snippet: Congestive heart failure (69%, 95% CI: 56-80%) and pulmonary hypertension (23%, 95% CI: 14-36%) were the main non-fatal comorbidities in patients with HHT.

nodes.description: Endothelial cells carry roughly half the normal complement of endoglin, an accessory protein of the TGF-beta receptor superfamily that is highly expressed on endothelium. Mutant protein is largely absent from the cell surface, so the phenotype follows from reduced dosage of the wild-type product rather than from a dominant-negative species.

nodes.description: Mice carrying one inactivated endoglin allele reproduce the haploinsufficient state of HHT1. Some heterozygotes develop telangiectases or recurrent nosebleeds, and the fact that only some do - and that this depends on strain background - is the model's principal contribution: it demonstrates that modifier genes and epigenetic factors, not the ENG lesion alone, govern expressivity. Homozygous null embryos die at gestational day 10.0-10.5 with failed vascular plexus maturation and arrested heart development, defining the null phenotype against which haploinsufficiency is read.

Bleeding from gastrointestinal mucosal telangiectases, rarely seen before age 50 years. Unlike the pulmonary and cerebral lesions, this is the one major manifestation reported as less frequent in HHT1 than in HHT2 (6.5% versus 16.4%).

nodes.description: Endoglin acts as a co-receptor alongside ALK1, the ACVRL1 gene product, in the endothelial BMP9 pathway that phosphorylates SMAD1/5/8. Reduced endoglin lowers signalling through this axis. That ENG and ACVRL1 lesions converge on one pathway is the accepted explanation for why HHT1 and HHT2 are clinically similar disorders despite different genes.

nodes.description: The defining lesion of HHT is an arteriovenous malformation that lacks intervening capillaries, so an artery drains directly into a vein. Small lesions of this kind are the mucocutaneous telangiectases; large ones are the visceral AVMs. Both the fragility that causes bleeding and the shunt physiology that causes the neurological complications follow from this single architectural change.

nodes.description: An immunomodulatory antiangiogenic agent. In the randomized, placebo-controlled PATH-HHT trial (NCT03910244), pomalidomide reduced Epistaxis Severity Score at 24 weeks by a mean of 0.94 points more than placebo; the trial was stopped early at a planned interim analysis for efficacy. Neutropenia, constipation and rash were more common on pomalidomide. The trial enrolled HHT patients without restricting to ENG genotype.

nodes.description: Pulmonary AVMs are the signature visceral lesion of HHT1 and are markedly more frequent here than in ACVRL1-related HHT2. They were found in 75% of HHT1 versus 44% of HHT2 patients on systematic imaging in one series, and symptomatic PAVMs in 34.4% of HHT1 versus 5.2% of HHT2 in a second. Because they bypass the pulmonary capillary filter, they create a right-to-left shunt rather than acting only as a bleeding source.

Neurological manifestations secondary to shunting were observed only in HHT1 patients in a systematically screened cohort, and respiratory symptoms were likewise mainly an HHT1 finding.

nodes.description: The germline variant is present in every cell, yet malformations form in only a small minority of vessels. A very-low-level somatic loss-of-function mutation on the second ENG allele within the lesional endothelium supplies the focal trigger. Loss of heterozygosity at ENG has been demonstrated in a brain AVM in which the germline and somatic loss-of-function mutations lay on different alleles. This node explains the focality and the intrafamilial variability that haploinsufficiency alone does not.
